16	## Mathematical constraints
17	
18	- Equating Steinberg top classes in degree 2g-2=10 with fundamental classes of maximal simplices of the curve complex. [reason: Dimension mismatch: the Steinberg module is the top reduced homology of the curve complex in degree 2g-2, while maximal simplices of the curve complex have dimension 3g-4=14 for g=6, not 2g-2.]
19	- Treating intersecting Humphries chains of 2g+1 curves as simplices of the curve complex C, and using them as Steinberg generators. [reason: Simplices of the curve complex require pairwise-disjoint curves; a Humphries generating set consists of intersecting curves and is not a simplex of C.]
20	- Inferring that every filling carrier is Mod_6-equivalent to a hyperelliptic chain from Mod_6-transitivity on Humphries chains. [reason: Transitivity on a special set of intersecting chains does not move arbitrary filling systems into hyperelliptic/symmetric position and does not generate all of St_6⊗Q by the Mod-orbit of im(b: St(Σ_{0,14})→St_6).]
21	- Concluding S^-=0 (hence (S⊗H^{⊗5})_{Sp}=0) from a fixed hyperelliptic involution acting as +id on a symmetric subcomplex C^{sym}, without a generation theorem for St_6 by hyperelliptic/Birman–Hilden classes. [reason: The central-sign argument only reduces Sp-coinvariants to the S^- summand; vanishing requires S^-=0, which needs a correct generation statement (or a Broaddus generator in that orbit), not mere +1 action on a symmetric subcomplex.]
22	- Using the standard ordered 0-filling class of 2g arcs as a cyclic generator of St fixed by handle half-turns to compute (St⊗V)_G. [reason: That class is zero in St; Broaddus cyclicity uses a different nontrivial generator φ0.]
23	- Invoking Church–Farb–Putman top-cohomology vanishing to conclude H^{19}(M_6;H^{⊗5})=0 for odd symplectic local systems. [reason: Church–Farb–Putman kill only trivial-coefficient top cohomology, not odd symplectic coefficients.]
24	- From the set-theoretic support statement V(J)=e(S) alone, conclude the ideal inclusion J subset I_e. [reason: Over a possibly nonreduced base, equality of reduced supports does not control nilpotents in the base.
